div.p: The township of Wandin Yalloak in the Yarra Valley was proclaimed in 1874. When Seville was proclaimed in 1885, Wandin Yalloak's name was changed to Redlands, but reverted in 1954 to Wandin Yallock, with the spelling changed from Yalloak to Yallock. The area was an important berry-growing district in the 19th century and one of the pioneering families was the Sebires. Mont de Lancey (1882), the restored house of the Sebire family, is an important tourist venue in the area, which is now part of Wandin North (3139).
